name: gizza-ai/wrap-lines-in-quotes
summary: Wrap each line of text in quotes or brackets

tool.description: Wrap each line of text in chosen quotes or brackets, with an optional trailing separator — great for turning a column of values into a SQL `IN (…)` list, JSON array, or CSV row. wrap picks the delimiter style: double "…" (default), single '…', backtick, paren (…), square […], curly {…}, angle <…>, guillemet «…», or custom (then open/close set your own delimiters; an empty close mirrors open). separator is appended after each wrapped line (e.g. `,`); by default the last wrapped line omits it (set last_line_separator=true to keep it). skip_empty (default true) leaves blank lines unchanged. trim strips surrounding whitespace per line; escape backslash-escapes the delimiter inside each line so the result stays valid. Returns the wrapped text plus total/wrapped line counts. Runs locally.

close.description: Closing delimiter when wrap=custom. Empty mirrors the opening delimiter. Ignored for presets.

escape.description: When true, backslash-escape the delimiter chars (and `\`) inside each line so the output is a valid quoted string. Default false.

last_line_separator.description: When true, the last wrapped line also gets the trailing separator. Default false (so a comma separator yields a valid IN(…)/array body).

open.description: Opening delimiter when wrap=custom (e.g. `<!--`). Ignored for presets.

separator.description: String appended after each wrapped line, e.g. `,` for a SQL IN-list or JSON array. Default none.

skip_empty.description: When true (default), blank/whitespace-only lines pass through unchanged — not wrapped, no separator.

text.description: The text whose lines should each be wrapped (split on newlines).

trim.description: When true, strip surrounding whitespace from each line before wrapping. Default false.

wrap.description: Delimiter style around each line: double "…", single '…', backtick `…`, paren (…), square […], curly {…}, angle <…>, guillemet «…», or custom (uses open/close). Default double.
